  "ppv": null,
  "npv": null,
  "endpoints_animal": [
    "pharmacological activity",
    "safety"
  ],
  "endpoints_human": [
    "tolerable dose ranges",
    "pharmacologically active dose ranges",
    "therapeutic efficacy"
  ],
  "endpoint_class": "mixed",
  "concordance_definition": "The overlap between preclinical and clinical well-tolerated dose levels and pharmacologically active dose ranges.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "limited number of included studies",
    "diversity of included studies",
    "non-randomness of included studies (only studies from own research institute)",
    "used linear inter- and extrapolation to determine missing pharmacokinetic parameters",
    "analysis limited to studies of unregistered compounds mostly in healthy volunteers",
    "IBS are all investigators have at their disposal when they study the pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and tolerability of a new CNS active compound."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "DVG reports personal fees from Danone Nutricia Research B.V. and MSD Animal Health outside of the submitted work. GSF reports personal fees from Merck KGaA, Curare Consulting B.V., Access to Medicine Foundation, 3D PharmXchange B.V. and Janssen Biologics B.V. outside of the submitted work. None of the other authors has any conflict of interest.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "25 studies met the inclusion criteria",
    "12 (48%) of the included studies concerned a First-in-Human (FIH) study",
    "In 8 of the 25 IBs (32%) a rationale for the chosen animal model was provided",
    "In none of the IBs pharmacokinetic reporting was complete for all in vivo pharmacology experiments",
    "None of the preclinical experiments in the included IBs fulfilled the criteria of internal validity",
    "In most studies (N = 22, 88%), the starting dose (HLR AE ) for the clinical study was at least a (rounded) factor 10 below the HED of the NOAEL",
    "For HED, the human upper tolerability range HUR AE surpassed the NOAEL in 9 out of 25 studies (36%)",
    "For C max , the HUR AE surpassed the C max value of the NOAEL in 8 of the 25 studies (32%)",
    "For AUC, the HUR AE surpassed the AUC associated with the NOAEL in 12 out of 23 studies (52%)",
    "16% of clinical studies reporting unacceptable side effects at values below the NOAEL was similar for all three exposure parameters",
    "Eight (32%) IBs (IB2, IB5, IB6, IB8, IB18, IB22, IB23, IB24, IB25) reported statistically significant pharmacological effects at the lowest tested preclinical dose",
    "Nine (36%) clinical studies (IB1, IB13, IB14, IB15, IB16, IB19, IB20, IB21, IB23) showed a pharmacological effect at all administered doses",
    "On average, HED was the best predictor of pharmacologically active ranges, with 84% overlap between preclinical and clinical pharmacologically active ranges",
    "AUC was the best predictor with 83% of the compounds having more than 80% overlap",
    "Overall, the preclinical data predicted the pharmacologically active range in humans to a high degree, as indicated by an overlap of ≥ 80% in 18 out of 25 (72%) for HED, 15 out of 25 (60%) for C max and 19 out of 23 (83%) for AUC",
    "A particularly poor preclinical prediction of the clinical active range (as indicated by ≤ 20% overlap) was shown in 2 out of 25 studies (8%) for HED, 7 of 25 (28%) for C max and 4 out of 23 studies (17%) for AUC",
    "Therapeutic efficacy study results were reported for only six of the 25 included compounds",
    "In 58% of the included studies, the starting dose for the clinical study was based on preclinical safety experiments (NOAEL) only",
    "In all studies included in this report, the observed adverse events were exaggerated pharmacological effects in line with the working mechanism of the compound and therefore predictable based on preclinical data."
  ]
}
